title: Separate June DMI slopes gave no clear autumn forecast gain in 1981-2024
abstract: We tested whether separate slopes for positive and negative June Indian Ocean Dipole Mode Index (DMI) improve September-November DMI forecasts. We used fixed NOAA HadISST1.1 and ERSSTv5 index files. Each fit used only earlier years from 1950. Both models included June DMI, June Nino 3.4 and a linear time trend. The added model used absolute June DMI. In 44 test years from 1981 to 2024, this term raised mean squared error by 3.14%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -8.27% to +0.26%. RMSE rose from 0.31764 to 0.32258 degrees C. All planned checks had negative point gains. The first training set had only seven positive June states. The result gives no clear gain for this fixed hinge. It does not reject physical IOD asymmetry. Revised data, short records, simple models and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate scores, a figure and separate external-data retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: MSE reduction from separate June DMI slopes. Bars give conditional 95% block intervals. Positive values mean added skill. All point estimates are negative.

citations.reason: Shared sources and June-to-autumn benchmark. We test a fixed hinge against its stronger trend baseline; evidence overlaps.
